messages.subject: Re: summary not printing fully
parts:
Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

I also wonder whether you are using Rstudio? It seems that Rstudio does some package loading things that are different from regular R.

Thanks,
Ed

Don't if it can help. I have a case that can reproduce the problem on my Windows machine, using Rgui, VS Code, and RStudio.

First, in a fresh session, run the following *without* loading blavaan:

# Code begins here
set.seed(8740325)
sigma <- matrix(.8, 4, 4)
diag(sigma) <- 1
dat <- MASS::mvrnorm(100, mu = c(x1 = 0, x2 = 0, x3 = 0, x4 = 0),
                          Sigma = sigma)
dat <- as.data.frame(dat)
mod <- "f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4"
fit <- blavaan::bcfa(model = mod,
                     data = dat,
                     n.chains = 2)
summary(fit)
# Code ends here

This error will occur after the call blavaan::bcfa()

Error in blavaan(model = mod, data = dat, n.chains = 2, model.type = "bcfa", : could not find function "blavaan"

This is the search path:

> search()
[1] ".GlobalEnv"        "package:stats"     "package:graphics"  "package:grDevices" "package:utils"    
[6] "package:datasets"  "package:methods"   "Autoloads"         "package:base"  

Then run the code again, in the *same session*, with blavaan loaded:

# Code begins here

On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 12:25:51 AM UTC+8 Ed Merkle wrote:
Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

I also wonder whether you are using Rstudio? It seems that Rstudio does some package loading things that are different from regular R.

Thanks,
Ed

A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.

-- Shu Fai

Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

I also wonder whether you are using Rstudio? It seems that Rstudio does some package loading things that are different from regular R.

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 05:24 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:

A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.

-- Shu Fai

On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 12:25:51 AM UTC+8 Ed Merkle wrote:
Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

I also wonder whether you are using Rstudio? It seems that Rstudio does some package loading things that are different from regular R.

Thanks,
Ed

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, burnin=100, sample=100)

summary(fit)

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 05:24 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:

A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.

-- Shu Fai

On Wednesday, February 15, 2023 at 12:25:51 AM UTC+8 Ed Merkle wrote:
Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

I also wonder whether you are using Rstudio? It seems that Rstudio does some package loading things that are different from regular R.

Thanks,
Ed

parts:
Thanks for this example. I created a few more examples based on this one that hopefully may give some hints on the problem. All examples produced by reprex(). To run them in an interactive R session, they should be run in a fresh session.

This is the normal case, library(blavaan) only:

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(blavaan)
#> Loading required package: lavaan
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
#> Loading required package: Rcpp
#> This is blavaan 0.4-6
#> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
#>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="blavaan"
#> object="blavFitIndices"
#> object="blavPPMC"
#> object="diagonalMatrix"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"
#> object="sparseMatrix"
#> object="stanfit"

The summary method for blavaan is available, as expected.

The following example uses loadNamespace("blavaan") first and then library(blavaan):

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
loadNamespace("blavaan")
#> <environment: namespace:blavaan>
showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(blavaan)
#> Loading required package: lavaan
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
#> Loading required package: Rcpp
#> This is blavaan 0.4-6
#> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
#>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="diagonalMatrix"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"
#> object="sparseMatrix"
#> object="stanfit"

First, just loading the namespace does not make the method for blavaan available.
Second, if the namespace of blavaan is loaded first, even when blavaan is loaded by library(), the summary method for blavaan is not loaded.

Interestingly, this is not the case for lavaan, as shown in the following example:

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
loadNamespace("lavaan")
#> <environment: namespace:lavaan>
showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"

Similarly, loading the namespace of lavaan does not make its summary method available.
However, the summary method of lavaan is available after library(lavaan) even if it is run after loadNamespace.

So, it seems that the problem occurs for blavaan but not for lavaan. Maybe something in addition to loading the namespace first.

Not shown above but I notice a similar problem with predict(), which is available in both lavaan and blavaan.

Maybe something about method dispatch? I would love to learn more about this case.

-- Shu Fai

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 05:24 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:
A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.

-- Shu Fai

Thanks for the report, and it is indeed a problem that I have not been able to reproduce/diagnose. In the past, I have tweaked S3 and S4 summary methods to try to ensure that the blavaan method is used instead of lavaan. But the blavaan object "inherits" from lavaan, so that the lavaan summary() would be used if the blavaan method cannot be found. Maybe this could happen if you load a blavaan object without doing library(blavaan), but I can't imagine that everyone is doing that.

A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

Thanks, it seems that the problem disappears if I list lavaan in the "Imports" field instead of the "Depends" field of DESCRIPTION.

By listing it in Imports, I think that people would not be able to automatically run other lavaan commands on a blavaan object. This might be a good thing, but I need to do more testing to figure out if this change would break anything.

Ed

Thanks for this example. I created a few more examples based on this one that hopefully may give some hints on the problem. All examples produced by reprex(). To run them in an interactive R session, they should be run in a fresh session.

This is the normal case, library(blavaan) only:

showMethods("summary")

#> object="lavaanList"

The summary method for blavaan is available, as expected.

The following example uses loadNamespace("blavaan") first and then library(blavaan):

showMethods("summary")

#> Loading required package: lavaan

#> Loading required package: Rcpp
#> This is blavaan 0.4-6
#> On multicore systems, we suggest use of future::plan("multicore") or
#>   future::plan("multisession") for faster post-MCMC computations.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="diagonalMatrix"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"
#> object="sparseMatrix"
#> object="stanfit"

First, just loading the namespace does not make the method for blavaan available.
Second, if the namespace of blavaan is loaded first, even when blavaan is loaded by library(), the summary method for blavaan is not loaded.

Interestingly, this is not the case for lavaan, as shown in the following example:

showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
loadNamespace("lavaan")
#> <environment: namespace:lavaan>
showMethods("summary")
#>
#> Function "summary":
#>  <not an S4 generic function>
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-14
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
showMethods("summary")
#> Function: summary (package base)
#> object="ANY"
#> object="lavaan"
#> object="lavaanList"
#> object="mle"

Similarly, loading the namespace of lavaan does not make its summary method available.
However, the summary method of lavaan is available after library(lavaan) even if it is run after loadNamespace.

So, it seems that the problem occurs for blavaan but not for lavaan. Maybe something in addition to loading the namespace first.

Not shown above but I notice a similar problem with predict(), which is available in both lavaan and blavaan.

Maybe something about method dispatch? I would love to learn more about this case.

-- Shu Fai

On Wed, 2023-02-15 at 05:24 -0800, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:
A quick followup, may or may not be related.

The error in the first run of my example, using blavaan::cfa() with out library(blavaan), is probably due to the following line:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/028556627c571d65fc8f237ef8bffa6c88cdf024/R/blavaan.R#L1061

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

Error occurred because blavaan is not in the search path, even though blavaan::cfa() is executed without problem.

This is the corresponding line in lavaan:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/17b67023c8816e041012da63ad57240f99c71ef3/R/xxx_lavaan.R#L2153

mc[[1L]] <- quote(lavaan::lavaan)

"lavaan::" is added. This makes sense because "lavaan::cfa()" and " "lavaan::sem()" are valid ways to call these functions (afaik, are also preferred ways to call them inside a package).

Not sure if changing

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan)

to

mc[[1L]] <- quote(blavaan::blavaan)

will remove the problem of summary() in my example. I failed to compile the Rcpp code in my computer and so I could not test this in a fork.

If this can solve the problem in my example, maybe it can shed light on why that problem occurred in other scenarios.

-- Shu Fai
